title: On‑Prem Upgrade Sequencer and Rollback Simulator for Private Deployments
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Customers running Redwood Private (VPC / on‑prem) require predictable upgrade behavior across heterogeneous fleets. Existing upgrade flows are manual or ad-hoc: DB schema migrations sometimes require orchestration across services, some upgrades need ordering constraints (eg. control plane first, agents second), and rollback plans are rarely exercised. This ticket scopes a new upgrade 'sequencer' service plus a rollback simulator that together reduce upgrade risk for Private customers.

Goals:
- Implement an upgrade sequencer that models a release as an ordered DAG of steps (control plane, agents, database migrations, data-plane components, post-checks) and drives execution across customer environments.
- Provide a rollback simulator that runs a dry-run of upgrade+rollback paths against a sandbox topology and surfaces likely failure points (migration blockers, ordering violations, incompatible versions).
- Integrate sequencer with LTS / channel metadata so customers can opt into LTS patches vs rolling feature releases.
- Add rollout gates (canary subsets, health-check windows, QA approvals, automatic fallback to last-known-good) that are configurable per-deployment.
- Deliver observability: per-step logs, tokenized cost estimate, and a post-upgrade report that maps checks to release notes.

Scope (in-scope): sequencer runtime API, migration step primitives (schema-migration, config-change, agent-update, service-restart), rollout gate primitives (canary, health-check, time-window, manual-approval), rollback simulator that consumes a release manifest and emits a risk report. Integration adapters for Private control plane to trigger agent rollouts and for the upgrade database migration runner.

Out-of-scope: full UI in Console (we'll provide APIs and CLI hooks), automated cross-customer multi-tenant coordination, support for air-gapped manual image transfer (handled separately).

Constraints and non-goals: sequencer must not assume homogeneous cluster topology — support mixed agent versions and partial connectivity. Migrations that are destructive require operator confirmation. All control-plane actions must be audited for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Sequencer exposes a stable REST/GRPC API to submit a ReleaseManifest and returns a run_id synchronously.
Sequencer can represent and execute a release DAG with at least these step types: control-plane-update, agent-update, schema-migration, config-apply, traffic-shift, post-check.
Rollback simulator produces a human-readable risk report that lists probable blocking steps, with severity and remediation suggestions, for a provided ReleaseManifest.
A canary gate that routes 1% and then 10% traffic windows can be defined and executed automatically with health-check thresholds and automatic rollbacks on failure.
Sequencer emits structured events compatible with Console tracing and creates an audit entry for every step (who/what/when/outcome).

End-to-end test: run sequencer against a staging Private deployment using a stateful schema migration + agent binary update; the sequencer completes, and rollback path can be executed to restore pre-upgrade state in under the defined RTO for the test.
Documentation: API reference, sample ReleaseManifest templates, and a runbook for common failure scenarios are published in Confluence and linked in the post-upgrade report.
migration_plan_summary: ReleaseManifest will version steps with semantic step-ids and required preconditions. Database migrations must be idempotent and marked with migration-phases (precopy, apply, verify, vacuum). Sequencer will coordinate a 'precopy' where heavy index builds or data copies are warmed on target nodes before the main apply. For stateful services, the sequencer will execute an agent drain, apply, and un-drain pattern. Rollback simulator will analyze manifests to find irreversible steps and flag them. All migrations are executed inside a transaction-safe window where possible, otherwise a compensating migration is recorded.
rollout_gates: Health-check gate: check service latency/success-rate vs baseline with z-score threshold
Schema-compatibility gate: verify consumers against new schema using a compatibility check tool
Manual approval gate: blocks progress until operator approves via CLI or Console API
Auto-fallback gate: if N consecutive post-check failures occur, trigger automated rollback to previous release_id
testing_plan: Unit tests for sequencer state machine transitions and step retries
Integration test harness that runs sequencer against a 3-node Private staging cluster (control plane + 2 agents) with a sample schema migration
Chaos testing: introduce agent flakiness and verify sequencer retry/backoff/rollback behavior
Simulator validation: run rollback simulator reports against historical upgrade incidents and validate that simulator would have flagged the root cause
E2E performance test to validate sequencer can schedule 100 small-step releases per hour without saturating control-plane resources

2026-03-08 - Liam Rodriguez: Hooked sequencer to the Private control-plane API. Need to add stronger idempotency guarantees for agent-update step (currently re-sends image tag).
2026-03-10 - QA: Found a race in schema-migration when pre-copy is interrupted by agent restart. Added 'precopy-coordinator' to migration primitives as a mitigation.
2026-03-11 - Security: auditing requirements clarified — sequencer must sign release manifests with org key and persist run metadata to the compliance store.
2026-03-12 - Liam Rodriguez: Began building rollback simulator heuristics (detect irreversible DDL, missing compensating migration). Next: integrate with historical incident corpus.
